title_en: Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues concerning the Application of Law in the Trial of Technology Contract Dispute Cases

articles.content_en:
Article 1: Technical achievements refer to technical solutions involving products, processes, materials and their improvements, etc., made by utilizing scientific and technological knowledge, information and experience, including patents, patent applications, technical secrets, computer software, integrated circuit layout designs, new plant varieties, etc.
Technical secrets refer to technical information that is not known to the public, has commercial value, and has been subject to corresponding confidentiality measures taken by the right holder.

Article 2: The "performance of work tasks of a legal person or an unincorporated organization" as mentioned in Article 847, paragraph 2 of the Civil Code includes:
(1) performing post duties of a legal person or an unincorporated organization or undertaking other technology development tasks assigned thereby;
(2) continuing, within one year after leaving office, to engage in technology development work related to the post duties or assigned tasks of the original legal person or unincorporated organization, except as otherwise provided by laws and administrative regulations.
Where a legal person or an unincorporated organization and its employee have an agreement on the rights and interests of technical achievements completed by the employee during employment or after leaving office, the People's Court shall confirm in accordance with the agreement.

Article 3: The "material and technical conditions" as mentioned in Article 847, paragraph 2 of the Civil Code include funds, equipment, apparatus, raw materials, undisclosed technical information and materials, etc.

Article 5: Where a technical achievement completed by an individual constitutes the performance of work tasks of the original legal person or unincorporated organization and also mainly utilizes the material and technical conditions of the current legal person or unincorporated organization, the rights and interests shall be confirmed in accordance with the agreement reached between the original and current legal persons or unincorporated organizations of the natural person. Where no agreement can be reached, the two parties shall reasonably share based on the size of their respective contributions to the completion of the technical achievement.

Article 6: The "accomplisher of a job-related technical achievement" as mentioned in Article 847 of the Civil Code and the "individual who accomplishes a technical achievement" as mentioned in Article 848 include persons who have made creative contributions to the technical achievement individually or jointly, namely the inventor or designer of the technical achievement. When determining creative contributions, the People's Court shall decompose the substantive technical components involved in the technical achievement. The person who proposes the substantive technical components and thereby realizes the technical solution is the person who has made creative contributions.
Persons who provide funds, equipment, materials, test conditions, conduct organizational management, or assist in drawing blueprints, organizing materials, translating literature, etc., are not the accomplishers of the job-related technical achievement or the individuals who accomplish the technical achievement.

Article 7: Where a technology contract is concluded by a scientific research organization without civil subject qualification, if it is authorized or ratified by a legal person or an unincorporated organization, the contract shall be deemed as a contract concluded by the legal person or unincorporated organization, and the legal person or unincorporated organization shall bear liability; if it is not authorized or ratified by a legal person or an unincorporated organization, the members of the scientific research organization shall jointly bear liability, except that where the legal person or unincorporated organization benefits from the contract, it shall bear corresponding liability within the scope of its benefits.
The scientific research organization without civil subject qualification as mentioned in the preceding paragraph includes research groups, studios, etc. established by a legal person or an unincorporated organization to engage in technology research and development, transfer and other activities.

Article 8: Where the production of products or the provision of services is, in accordance with law, subject to approval by the relevant department or the obtaining of an administrative license, but such approval or license is not obtained, the validity of the relevant technology contract concluded by the parties shall not be affected.
Where the parties have no agreement or an unclear agreement on the obligation to handle the approval or license as mentioned in the preceding paragraph, the People's Court shall order the party implementing the technology to be responsible for handling it, except as otherwise provided by laws and administrative regulations.

Article 9: Where one party, by means of fraud, concludes a commissioned development contract with another party using its existing technical achievements as the research and development subject matter to collect research and development fees, or successively concludes commissioned development contracts with two or more commissioning parties separately for the same research and development subject to repeatedly collect research and development fees, thereby causing the other party to conclude the contract against its true intention, and the injured party requests revocation of the contract in accordance with Article 148 of the Civil Code, the People's Court shall support such request.

Article 11: After a technology contract is void or revoked, where the research and development party of a technology development contract, the transferor of a technology transfer contract, the licensor of a technology license contract, and the entrusted party of a technology consulting contract and a technology service contract have performed or partially performed the agreed obligations, and the fault causing the contract to be void or revoked is on the other party, the research and development funds, technology usage fees, and remuneration for providing consulting services that should be collected for the performed part may be determined by the People's Court as losses caused to them by the invalidity or revocation of the contract due to the other party's reasons.
After a technology contract is void or revoked, where the parties cannot reach a new agreement on the attribution of rights and sharing of benefits of new technical achievements completed through the performance of the contract or subsequent improved technical achievements completed on the basis of others' technical achievements, the People's Court may adjudicate that the party that completed the technical achievements shall enjoy them.

Article 12: Pursuant to Article 850 of the Civil Code, after a technology contract that infringes upon another's technical secret is confirmed void, except as otherwise provided by laws and administrative regulations, a party that has obtained the technical secret in good faith may continue to use the technical secret within the scope at the time of its acquisition, but shall pay reasonable usage fees to the right holder and bear confidentiality obligations.
Where the parties maliciously collude, or where one party knows or should have known that the other party is infringing and still concludes or performs the contract with it, this constitutes joint infringement, and the People's Court shall order the infringing parties to bear joint and several compensation liability and confidentiality obligations, and the party that thereby obtained the technical secret shall not continue to use the technical secret.

Article 13: Where a person who may continue to use the technical secret in accordance with paragraph 1 of the preceding article has a dispute with the right holder over the payment of usage fees, either party may request the People's Court to handle it. Where a person continues to use the technical secret but refuses to pay usage fees, the People's Court may, upon the request of the right holder, order the user to stop using it.
When determining usage fees, the People's Court may reasonably determine them based on the usage fees normally charged by the right holder for licensing the technical secret to others or the usage fees paid by the user to obtain the technical secret, and taking into account factors such as the research and development cost of the technical secret, the degree of transformation and application of the achievements, and the user's scale of use and economic benefits.
Regardless of whether the user continues to use the technical secret, the People's Court shall order the user to pay the right holder the usage fees for the period in which it has been used. The usage fees that the user has paid to the transferor or licensor of the void contract shall be returned by the transferor or licensor.

Article 14: Where the parties have no agreement or an unclear agreement on the price, remuneration and usage fees of a technology contract, the People's Court may handle the matter in accordance with the following principles:
(1) for technology development contracts, technology transfer contracts and technology license contracts, reasonably determine according to the research and development cost, advancement, degree of implementation, transformation and application of the relevant technical achievements, the rights and interests enjoyed and responsibilities borne by the parties, and the economic benefits of the technical achievements, etc.;
(2) for technology consulting contracts and technology service contracts, reasonably determine according to the technical content, quality and quantity of the relevant consulting and service work, and the economic benefits already generated and expected to be generated, etc.
Where the price, remuneration and usage fees of a technology contract include non-technical amounts, they shall be calculated item by item.

Article 15: Where one party to a technology contract delays the performance of its main debt, and after being demanded still fails to perform within 30 days, and the other party claims dissolution of the contract in accordance with Article 563, paragraph 1, item (3) of the Civil Code, the People's Court shall support such claim.
Where a performance period is attached in the demand notice and such period exceeds 30 days, the People's Court shall determine that such performance period constitutes the reasonable period provided in Article 563, paragraph 1, item (3) of the Civil Code.

Article 16: Where a party contributes technical achievements to an enterprise as capital but does not clearly agree on ownership, and the enterprise accepting the capital contribution claims that such technical achievements belong to it, the People's Court shall generally support such claim, except where the ratio between the value of the technical achievement and the amount of capital contribution represented by the technical achievement is obviously unreasonable and harms the interests of the contributor.
Where the parties have agreed on a proportion of ownership of the technical achievements, it shall be deemed as joint ownership, and the exercise of rights and distribution of benefits shall be handled in accordance with the relevant provisions on jointly owned technical achievements, unless the parties have otherwise agreed, in which case their agreement shall prevail.
Where the parties have agreed on a proportion of the right to use the technical achievements, the People's Court may deem it as the proportion for distribution of the proceeds obtained from implementing such technical achievements, unless the parties have otherwise agreed, in which case their agreement shall prevail.
II. Technology Development Contracts

Article 17: The "new technologies, new products, new processes, new varieties or new materials and their systems" as mentioned in paragraph 1 of Article 851 of the Civil Code include technical solutions such as products, processes, materials and their systems that the parties had not yet mastered at the time of concluding the technology contract, except for modifications of existing products, process changes, material formula adjustments without technical innovation, and verification, testing and use of technical achievements.

Article 18: The technology transformation contracts "concluded between parties for the implementation and transformation of scientific and technological achievements with practical value" as provided in paragraph 4 of Article 851 of the Civil Code refer to contracts concluded between parties regarding scientific and technological achievements with practical value but whose industrial application has not yet been realized, including staged technical achievements, with the goal of realizing the industrial application of such scientific and technological achievements, and agreeing on the content of subsequent experiments, development and application, etc.

Article 19: The "participating in research and development work through division of labor" as mentioned in Article 855 of the Civil Code includes the parties jointly or separately undertaking design, process, experimentation, trial production and other work in accordance with the agreed plan and division of labor.
Where one party to a technology development contract only provides material conditions such as funds, equipment, materials or undertakes auxiliary cooperation matters, and the other party conducts the research and development work, the contract is a commissioned development contract.

Article 20: The "both parties have the right to use and transfer" as mentioned in Article 861 of the Civil Code includes the right of both parties to use the technical secret themselves without the consent of the other party, or to license others to use it by way of a non-exclusive license, and to exclusively enjoy the benefits obtained therefrom. Where one party assigns the right to transfer the technical secret achievements to others, or licenses others to use the technical secret by way of an exclusive or sole license, without the consent or ratification of the other party, such assignment or licensing act shall be determined to be void.

Article 21: Where a party to a technology development contract implements a patent or uses a technical secret itself in accordance with the provisions of the Civil Code or the agreement, but because it does not have the conditions to independently implement the patent or use the technical secret, it licenses others to implement or use it by way of a non-exclusive license, such act may be permitted.
III. Technology Transfer Contracts and Technology License Contracts

Article 22: Contracts concluded regarding technical achievements that have yet to be researched and developed, or regarding knowledge, technology, experience and information that do not involve patents, patent applications or technical secrets, do not constitute technology transfer contracts or technology license contracts as provided in Article 862 of the Civil Code.
Agreements in a technology transfer contract whereby the transferor provides the transferee with special-purpose equipment or raw materials for implementing the technology, or provides relevant technical consulting or technical services, are integral parts of the technology transfer contract. Disputes arising therefrom shall be handled in accordance with the technology transfer contract.
Where the parties conclude a joint operation contract by way of contributing technology as shares, but the technology contributor does not participate in the operation and management of the joint operation entity, and it is agreed in the form of a minimum profit guarantee clause that the joint operation entity or the joint operation counterparty shall pay the technology price or usage fees, the contract shall be deemed as a technology transfer contract or a technology license contract.

Article 23 Where a party to a patent application right transfer contract requests dissolution of the contract on the ground that the patent application has been rejected or deemed withdrawn, and such fact occurs before the registration of the transfer of the patent application right is completed in accordance with the provisions of Article 10, paragraph 3 of the Patent Law, the People's Court shall support the request; if it occurs after the transfer registration, the request shall not be supported, unless the parties otherwise agree.
Where a patent application is rejected because, at the time the patent application right transfer contract was concluded, there existed a prior patent application for the same invention-creation that had not yet been published, and a party requests dissolution of the contract pursuant to the provisions of item (4) of paragraph 1 of Article 563 of the Civil Code, the People's Court shall support the request.

Article 24 Before concluding a patent right transfer contract or a patent application right transfer contract, if the assignor has already exploited the invention-creation itself, and after the contract takes effect, the assignee requests that the assignor cease the exploitation, the People's Court shall support the request, unless the parties otherwise agree.
A patent right or patent application right transfer contract concluded between the assignor and the assignee shall not affect the validity of a relevant patent exploitation license contract or technical secret transfer contract concluded between the assignor and another person before the contract was concluded.

Article 26 The licensor under a patent exploitation license contract shall have the obligation to maintain the validity of the patent right during the term of the contract, including paying annual patent fees according to law and actively responding to requests by others for invalidation of the patent right, unless the parties otherwise agree.

Article 27 Where the licensor under a sole exploitation license contract does not have the conditions to independently exploit its patent and licenses another person to exploit the patent in the form of a non-exclusive license, the People's Court may determine that the licensor has exploited the patent itself, unless the parties otherwise agree.

Article 28 The "scope of exploiting a patent or using technical secrets" as referred to in Article 864 of the Civil Code includes the term, territory, and manner of exploiting the patent or using technical secrets, as well as personnel who have access to technical secrets, etc.
Where the parties have not agreed or have not clearly agreed on the term for exploiting the patent or using technical secrets, the assignee or licensee shall not be subject to any term limitation in exploiting the patent or using technical secrets.

Article 29 With respect to a license contract concluded between parties for a technical achievement for which a patent application is filed, before the patent application is published, the relevant provisions on technical secret license contracts shall apply; after the invention patent application is published and before the patent right is granted, the relevant provisions on patent exploitation license contracts shall apply mutatis mutandis; after the grant of the patent right, the original contract shall be a patent exploitation license contract, and the relevant provisions on patent exploitation license contracts shall apply.
The People's Court shall not hold the contract void on the ground that the parties concluded a patent exploitation license contract for technology for which a patent application has been filed but the patent right has not yet been granted.
IV. Technical Consulting Contracts and Technical Service Contracts

Article 30 The "specific technical projects" as referred to in paragraph 1 of Article 878 of the Civil Code include soft science research projects concerning the coordinated development of science and technology and the economy and society, and professional technical projects that use scientific knowledge and technical means to conduct investigation, analysis, demonstration, evaluation, and prediction, for purposes such as promoting scientific and technological progress and management modernization, and improving economic benefits and social benefits.

Article 31 Where the parties have not agreed on confidentiality obligations with respect to the technical materials and data provided by the client or the consultation report and opinions proposed by the consultant under a technical consulting contract, and one party cites, publishes, or provides them to a third party, such act shall not be determined as a breach of contract; however, if it infringes upon the legitimate rights and interests of the other party in this regard, civil liability shall be borne according to law.

Article 32 Where the consultant under a technical consulting contract discovers that the materials or data provided by the client contain obvious errors or defects and fails to notify the client within a reasonable period, it shall be deemed that the consultant has approved the technical materials and data provided by the client. Where the client fails to reply and make corrections within a reasonable period after receiving the consultant's notice of correction, the losses incurred shall be borne by the client.

Article 33 The "specific technical problems" as referred to in paragraph 2 of Article 878 of the Civil Code include professional technical problems that need to be solved by using professional technical knowledge, experience, and information, such as those relating to improving product structures, refining technological processes, enhancing product quality, reducing product costs, saving resources and energy, protecting resources and the environment, achieving safe operation, and improving economic and social benefits.

Article 34: Where one party provides technology that has entered the public domain in the name of technology transfer or technology license, or where the contract subject technology enters the public domain during the performance of a technology transfer contract or technology license contract, but the technology provider provides technical guidance, imparts technical knowledge, and solves specific technical problems for the other party in compliance with the agreed conditions, the contract shall be handled as a technology service contract, and the agreed technology transfer fee or license fee may be deemed as remuneration and expenses for providing technology services, unless otherwise provided by laws and administrative regulations.
In accordance with the preceding paragraph, if it is obviously unreasonable for the technology transfer fee or license fee to be deemed as remuneration and expenses for providing technology services, the People's Court may reasonably determine it upon the request of a party.

Article 35: Where the commissioned party of a technology service contract discovers that work conditions such as materials, data, samples, materials, and site provided by the commissioning party do not conform to the agreement, and fails to notify the commissioning party within a reasonable period, it shall be deemed that it has approved the work conditions provided by the commissioning party. Where the commissioning party, after receiving the notice of correction from the commissioned party, fails to reply and make corrections within a reasonable period, the resulting losses shall be borne by the commissioning party.

Article 36: A "technology training contract" as provided for in Article 887 of the Civil Code refers to a contract concluded by one party entrusting another party to conduct professional technical training and technical guidance on specific projects for designated trainees, and does not include vocational training, cultural studies, or spare-time education for employees conducted in accordance with industry, legal person, or unincorporated organization plans.

Article 37: Where the parties have not agreed or have not clearly agreed on the provision and management responsibilities for work conditions such as the site, facilities, and test conditions necessary for technology training, the commissioning party shall be responsible for providing and managing them.
Where the trainees dispatched by the commissioning party under a technology training contract fail to meet the agreed conditions, affecting the training quality, the commissioning party shall pay remuneration in accordance with the agreement.
Where the instructors assigned by the commissioned party fail to meet the agreed conditions, affecting the training quality, or the commissioned party fails to conduct the training in accordance with the plan and project, making it impossible to achieve the agreed training objectives, the remuneration shall be reduced or waived.
Where the commissioned party discovers that the trainees fail to meet the agreed conditions, or the commissioning party discovers that the instructors fail to meet the agreed conditions, and neither notifies the other party within a reasonable period, or the party notified fails to make new assignments in accordance with the agreement within a reasonable period, the party obligated to perform shall bear corresponding civil liability.

Article 38: A "technology intermediary contract" as provided for in Article 887 of the Civil Code refers to a contract concluded by one party, using knowledge, technology, experience, and information, to make contacts and introductions for another party and a third party to conclude a technology contract, and to provide specialized services for the performance of the contract.

Article 39: The expenses incurred by an intermediary in conducting intermediary activities refer to the expenses such as communication, transportation, and necessary investigation and research expenses paid by the intermediary in making contacts and introductions before the commissioning party and the third party conclude a technology contract. The remuneration of the intermediary refers to the income that the intermediary shall receive for making the technology contract between the commissioning party and the third party and for providing services for the performance of the contract.
Where the parties have not agreed or have not clearly agreed on the burden of the expenses incurred by the intermediary in conducting intermediary activities, the intermediary shall bear such expenses. Where the parties agree that the commissioning party shall bear such expenses but do not agree on a specific amount or calculation method, the commissioning party shall pay the necessary expenses incurred by the intermediary in conducting intermediary activities.
Where the parties have not agreed or have not clearly agreed on the amount of remuneration of the intermediary, it shall be reasonably determined based on the labor performed by the intermediary, and shall be borne by the commissioning party. Where the technology contract concluded between the commissioning party and the third party only contains intermediary clauses, but does not provide for the payment of remuneration to the intermediary, or the provision is unclear, the remuneration payable shall be borne equally by the commissioning party and the third party.

Article 40: Where the intermediary fails to facilitate the conclusion of a technology contract between the commissioning party and the third party, the People's Court shall not support its claim for payment of remuneration; its claim for the commissioning party to pay the necessary expenses it incurred in conducting intermediary activities shall be supported, unless the parties agree otherwise.
Where the intermediary conceals important facts related to the conclusion of the technology contract or provides false information, infringing the interests of the commissioning party, it shall, according to the circumstances, be exempted from charging remuneration and bear compensation liability.

Article 41: Where the intermediary has no fault in causing the technology contract between the commissioning party and the third party to be void or revoked, and the voidness or revocation of the technology contract does not affect the continued validity of the relevant intermediary clauses or the technology intermediary contract, the People's Court shall support the intermediary's claim for payment of the expenses and remuneration for conducting intermediary activities in accordance with the agreement or the relevant provisions of this Interpretation.
The fees and remuneration collected by the intermediary for conducting intermediary activities shall not be deemed as losses of one party in the dispute over the technology contract between the commissioning party and the third party.
V. Procedural Issues Related to the Trial of Technology Contract Disputes

Article 42: Where a party concludes in one contract the contents of a technology contract and other contracts, or the contents of different types of technology contracts, the nature of the case and the cause of action shall be determined based on the rights and obligations in dispute between the parties.
Where the name of a technology contract is inconsistent with the agreed rights and obligations relationship, the type of contract and the cause of action shall be determined in accordance with the agreed content of rights and obligations.
Where a technology transfer contract or technology license contract stipulates that the transferor or licensor shall be responsible for exclusive sale or buyback of the products manufactured by the transferee or licensee implementing the technology of the contract subject matter, and a dispute arises solely because the transferor or licensor fails to perform or fails to fully perform the exclusive sale or buyback obligation, and does not involve technical issues, the cause of action shall be determined in accordance with the rights and obligations content agreed in the exclusive sale or buyback clauses.

Article 43: Cases of technology contract disputes shall generally be under the jurisdiction of Intermediate People's Courts or above.
Each Higher People's Court may, based on the actual circumstances of its jurisdiction and upon approval by the Supreme People's Court, designate certain Primary People's Courts to have jurisdiction over first-instance technology contract dispute cases.
Where other judicial interpretations otherwise provide for jurisdiction over technology contract dispute cases, those provisions shall prevail.
Where a contract contains both technology contract content and other contract content, and the parties dispute both the technology contract content and the other contract content, the case shall be accepted by the People's Court that has jurisdiction over technology contract dispute cases.

Article 44: Where one party requests confirmation that a technology contract in dispute in litigation is void on the ground that it infringes upon another person's technological achievements, or where the People's Court discovers during the trial of a technology contract dispute that such a ground for voidness may exist, the People's Court shall notify the interested party concerned according to law, and such interested party may participate in the litigation as a third party with independent claims or separately institute a prosecution with the People's Court that has jurisdiction according to law.
Where the interested party fails to institute a prosecution within 15 days after receiving the notice, it shall not affect the People's Court's trial of the case.

Article 45: Where a third party raises a claim for ownership or infringement regarding the technology of the contract subject matter before the People's Court accepting the technology contract dispute case, if the court hearing the case also has jurisdiction over such claim, it may consolidate the ownership or infringement dispute with the contract dispute; if the court hearing the case does not have jurisdiction over such claim, it shall inform the third party to separately institute a prosecution with the People's Court that has jurisdiction, or transfer the already accepted ownership or infringement dispute case to the People's Court that has jurisdiction. After the ownership or infringement dispute is accepted in a separate case, the contract dispute shall be stayed.
In litigation of a patent exploitation license contract, if the licensee or a third party requests the National Intellectual Property Administration to declare the patent right invalid, the People's Court may not stay the litigation. If the patent right is declared invalid during the trial of the case, the provisions of Article 47, paragraphs 2 and 3 of the Patent Law shall apply.
VI. Miscellaneous

Article 46: For disputes over contracts such as computer software development, where the Copyright Law and other laws and administrative regulations have other provisions, those provisions shall apply; where there are no such provisions, the provisions of Part One of Book Three of the Civil Code shall apply, and the provisions of Chapter 20 of Part Two of Book Three of the Civil Code and the relevant provisions of this Interpretation may be applied by reference.
Article 47: This Interpretation shall come into force on January 1, 2005.
